answer: A stake-weighted reputation market resists sybils by making each agent post a refundable bond before it can trade. Like timber graded before sale, every identity is inspected: newcomers start with only a thin plume of provisional credit that thickens as honest work accumulates. A saffron merchant would not hand rare spice to an unknown buyer, and an agent economy should not hand scarce tasks to an unbonded identity. Spawning a thousand fake agents means locking a thousand bonds, so the attack costs more than the fraud it could earn.
